causal_variable.definition: Degree to which other actors monopolize speaking turns, set agendas, and control conversational floor time.

inferred_variable.definition: The degree to which conversational floor time, agenda shaping, and response control are concentrated in a small subset of participants rather than distributed evenly across the meeting.
inferred_variable.evidence: Across the simulations, the participation structure shifts from relatively balanced turn-taking with natural pauses (033), to occasional short bursts of dominance by one speaker (034), to clear majority control by two or three recurring voices (035), and finally to near-monopolization by one or two senior participants who set topics and close threads unilaterally (036). By contrast, several background conditions remain stable across all four runs: the meeting stays on schedule, tone is terse and professional, agenda content is similar, and the subject agent often receives no reply or only minimal replies. This pattern shows that the systematically changing factor is not general meeting climate but the concentration of conversational control and available entry points for the subject agent.
